info.disambiguation: American hard rock band from Los Angeles
info.bio:
Guns N' Roses es una banda de hard rock que nació en Los Ángeles, en marzo de 1985. El grupo estaba formado por el cantante Axl Rose, los guitarristas Tracii Guns e Izzy Stradlin, el bajista Ole Beich, y el baterista Rob Gardner. El nombre deriva de la combinación de los seudónimos de Guns y Rose. Su primer concierto tuvo fecha el 26 de marzo de 1985 en el Troubador (Hollywood, California). 

Hollywood Rose fue la banda creada por Jeffrey Isabell (Izzy Stradlin) y William Rose (Axl Rose) después de dejar Lafayette

scenes.name: Conciertos y festivales: Donington y el negocio de la gira
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El concierto es, con el disco, el medio que siempre ha formado parte del metal y el más fiel a la relación entre artista y público. En los setenta los conciertos de heavy son un negocio seguro: llenan sin promoción y su público, pese al aspecto de Hell’s Angels, es fácil de manejar (los vigilantes de Chicago lo prefieren al de la música country). Hacia 1978 Black Sabbath, Rainbow, Judas Priest y UFO llenan grandes recintos, que necesitan mucho volumen y asientos sin tapizar. En los primeros ochenta llegan los festivales de metal como el de Donington, y tras el US Festival de 1983 el negocio florece: clubes dedicados, estadios al aire libre, festivales europeos de más de cien mil personas, patrocinio de cerveza y tabaco y el merchandising, que controla la banda y por el que ahora se sale de gira.

scenes.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El heavy metal renace en los mismos años que la new wave, aprovechando los sellos independientes: Motörhead (puente entre metal, Stooges/MC5 y punk), Judas Priest, Iron Maiden, Diamond Head, Def Leppard y, en EE UU, Van Halen. Entre 1982 y 1985 el subgénero gótico se convierte en «black metal» (Venom, Mercyful Fate, Celtic Frost, Helloween, Bathory). El pop-metal y el shock-rock (Twisted Sister, Mötley Crüe, Joan Jett, Bon Jovi, Savatage); la pompa y el doom (Manowar, Voivod, Saint Vitus, Pentagram); el metal progresivo (Living Colour, Queensrÿche, King's X, Pantera, Joe Satriani) y el «street sound» de Los Ángeles (Guns N' Roses, Jane's Addiction, Faster Pussycat).

podcast.title: Donington Crowd Collapse (August 28, 1988)
podcast.body: During Guns N' Roses' performance at a major outdoor rock show at a racetrack in Donington, England, on August 28, 1988, a crowd collapse occurred. Two men became trapped at the bottom of the pile, pushed so deeply into the mud that their deceased bodies had to be excavated. "During the gunner set, there was a crowd-collapse situation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Donington Park Crowd Collapse (1988)
podcast.body: During Guns N' Roses' set at a large outdoor show at Donington Park racetrack in England on August 28, 1988, a crowd collapse occurred. Two men died after being pulled from the pile, having been found face down in four inches of mud and requiring excavation. They were pronounced dead upon arrival at the hospital. "two bodies were pulled from a crowd collapse situation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 1992 MTV Music Video Awards Altercation
podcast.body: A backstage confrontation occurred at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards between Axl Rose, Kurt Cobain, and Courtney Love, where Axl reportedly told Kurt to "keep his woman in line." Separately, Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan and Nirvana bassist Chris Novoselic were also involved in a verbal dispute. "This boiled over to an altercation backstage at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards between Axel, Kurt and Courtney Love."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 1992 Overdose and Cardiac Arrest
podcast.body: In September 1992, while on tour with Metallica, Slash was staying in San Francisco before an Oakland gig. After the Oakland show, drug dealers came to his hotel room at 5 a.m., and Slash took a powerful speedball (heroin and cocaine). He collapsed in the hallway due to cardiac arrest and was technically dead for eight minutes. Paramedics revived him with an adrenaline needle. He was transported to the hospital but quickly signed himself out and was back on stage in Los Angeles two days later. "he'd been technically dead for eight minutes due to cardiac arrest."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Duff McKagan Pancreas Explosion (1994) – Near-Fatal Alcohol and Cocaine Abuse
podcast.body: Bassist Duff McKagan suffered what was described as a "explosion" of his pancreas in 1994 as a result of severe alcohol and cocaine abuse, causing third-degree internal burns and nearly killing him. The incident led to his complete sobriety, which he has maintained ever since. "Experienced an 'explosion' of his pancreas due to alcohol and cocaine abuse, causing third-degree internal burns and nearly killing him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Encounter with Kurt Cobain (1994)
podcast.body: After Kurt Cobain escaped rehab in April 1994, he was on Delta Flight 788 to Seattle and coincidentally sat next to Duff McKagan, the bassist for Guns N' Roses, who was also a "junkie rehab veteran." McKagan offered Cobain a ride upon landing, which Cobain refused. "Soon, he was on Delta Flight 788 to Seattle, and by sheer coincidence, he was sitting next to Guns & Roses bass player Duff McAgan, himself, a junkie we have veteran."

podcast.title: Former Members Form Velvet Revolver (2003)
podcast.body: Three former members of Guns N' Roses – Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum – reconciled and formed a new band, Velvet Revolver, in 2003, eventually recruiting Dave Kushner and Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band. It was Duff, Slash, and drummer Matt Sorom."

podcast.body: Velvet Revolver was described as "basically Guns and Roses with Scott Wyland and some other guy," highlighting the strong influence and presence of the former Guns N' Roses members in the supergroup's lineup. "It was basically guns and roses with Scott Wyland and some other guy."

podcast.title: Axl Rose Using Dave Grohl's Throne
podcast.body: In 2016, Axl Rose borrowed Dave Grohl's custom-built throne (which Grohl had used while touring with a broken leg) after Axl himself broke a bone in his foot, indicating a thawing of past hostilities between members of the two bands. "In fact, back in 2016, when Axel had a broken bone in his foot, he borrowed Dave Grohl's throne, the one he used to tour when Dave broke his leg."

podcast.title: Biggest Rock Comeback of the 2010s
podcast.body: Guns N' Roses, with 60% of their original lineup, reunited for the "Not in This Lifetime... Tour" between 2016 and 2019. This tour grossed nearly $600 million US dollars over 158 shows, making it the fourth-most profitable tour of all time to that point and the biggest rock comeback of the decade. "Even 60% of guns and roses reunited against all odds for the not-in-this-life-type tour, which grossed nearly $600 million US dollars over a hundred and fifty-eight shows played between 2016 and 2019, making it the fourth-most profitable tour of all time to that point." "That was easily the biggest rock come back at the decade."

podcast.title: Feud with Nirvana
podcast.body: The animosity began when Nirvana refused an offer to open for Guns N' Roses on a major world tour, a decision Kurt Cobain made due to concerns about being perceived as "sellouts" and his disdain for what he called the "typical Guns n' Roses type of band that has absolutely nothing to say." Axl Rose, a fan of Nirvana who even wore a Nirvana hat in the "Don't Cry" video, felt insulted and began publicly calling Kurt and Courtney Love "junkies," claiming their daughter had birth defects due to their drug use. "It began when Kurt refused an offer by the Gunners to have Nirvana open for them on one of their massive world tours."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Imperial Phase End
podcast.body: Guns N' Roses' imperial phase, which began in 1988-89, effectively ended by 1992. This conclusion was marked by singles like "Nightrain" and "You Could Be Mine" missing the top 10, and their cover of Paul McCartney's "Live and Let Die" becoming their third hit to miss the top 20, signaling the end of their "automatic cultural command." "Guns and Roses were still a major band, but the Imperial Phase, their time of automatic cultural command was over."

podcast.body: Guns N' Roses were among the artists influenced by Bad Brains, highlighting Bad Brains' significant impact on a diverse range of musicians. "So with the Beastie boys and the Chili Peppers and no doubt, and even Guns and Roses, that Bad Brains were great."

podcast.title: Manic Street Preachers' Self-Comparison
podcast.body: The Manic Street Preachers openly stated they felt they had more in common with bands like Guns N' Roses than with the emerging Britpop or Manchester music scene of the early 1990s. This reflected their preference for a more aggressive, American-style rock and roll. "They professed to have more in common with guns and roses in Motley Crew than anything from Manchester or early Britpop, saying that real rock and roll came from America."

podcast.title: Post-Overdose Heart Disease
podcast.body: About a decade after his 1992 overdose and cardiac arrest, Slash was diagnosed with heart disease. He subsequently received a pacemaker in 2004 to manage his condition. "About a decade later though, he was diagnosed with heart disease and ended up with a pacemaker in 2004."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Public Insults from Kurt Cobain
podcast.body: Kurt Cobain publicly characterized Axl Rose as "a sexist and a racist and a homophobic" in a late 1992 interview, stating that fans could not support both bands simultaneously and also criticized Guns N' Roses' songwriting. "Axel is a sexist and a racist and a homophobic. And you can't be on his side and be on our side."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reconciliation with Duff McKagan Before Kurt Cobain's Death
podcast.body: Days before his death, Kurt Cobain had a friendly chat with Duff McKagan on a Delta flight to Seattle, with McKagan offering him a ride from the airport. "Duff even offered Kurt a ride home from the airport, but before he had a chance to get in the car, Kurt vanished."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reunion for Touring
podcast.body: Guns N' Roses was one of many bands from past decades that reunited in the 21st century, a trend largely motivated by financial incentives. With declining CD sales impacting artist revenues, returning to the touring circuit offered a lucrative way to appeal to nostalgic fan bases and fill large venues. "The list of reunions is long."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

podcast.title: Second Chance Hits - General Mention
podcast.body: Guns and Roses are among the artists who have experienced "second chance hits" or "bringbacks," where singles initially flopped or did nothing on the charts before a catalyst propelled them to smash success. "Everyone from the Beatles to Prince, Guns and Roses to Taylor Swift has had one of these so-called bringbacks."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Tattoo Glorification in Hair Metal
podcast.body: Guns N' Roses is mentioned as a band that sang about tattoos and glorified them, fitting into the visual shock and appeal of the 80s hair metal era which included emphasis on hair, makeup, spandex, and distinctive footwear. "Guns and roses saying about tattoos. Molly crew is saying about getting tattooed. So in the 80s, bands like Molly crew, Guns and roses, LA guns, they glorify tattoos. Right up front."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Top-Grossing Tours
podcast.body: Guns N' Roses are cited as one of the legacy acts, with members typically aged 45 and above, that account for a significant portion of all-time top-grossing tours. Their continued success in filling arenas is attributed to the powerful pull of nostalgia, as fans are eager to relive their youth by attending their concerts.

podcast.body: Guns N' Roses toured with Living Color following the release and success of Living Color's debut album, "Vivid." "They toured with guns and roses and the rolling stones."

xref.title: Four Lead Singers – Bon Scott Died 1980, Brian Johnson Made Back in Black, Axl Rose Subbed in 2016
xref.body: AC/DC has had four lead singers. Dave Evans was the original, present from the band's 1973 formation through their glam-rock phase. Bon Scott replaced him after being discovered working as the band's chauffeur; he recorded seven albums cementing AC/DC's reputation but died of acute alcohol poisoning on February 19, 1980. Brian Johnson replaced him in time for *Back in Black* (1980), which has sold at least 50 million copies. When Johnson developed serious ear problems in 2016, Axl Rose of Guns N' Roses sang for approximately two dozen shows; Johnson subsequently received treatment and rejoined. "The swap worked way better than anyone could have dreamed."

"Soon, he was on Delta Flight 788 to Seattle, and by sheer coincidence, he was sitting next to Guns & Roses bass player Duff McAgan, himself, a junkie we have veteran."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Encounter with Kurt Cobain (April 1, 1994)
xref.body: Duff McKagan, the bassist for Guns N' Roses, coincidentally sat next to Kurt Cobain in business class on Delta Flight 788 as Cobain flew back to Seattle from Los Angeles. McKagan reported that Kurt seemed fine and even offered him a ride home from the airport, but Kurt declined, signed an autograph for two people, and then disappeared. "By coincidence, sitting next to him in business class was Guns and Roses' bass player, Duff McCagan. Duff says the Kurt seemed fine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Return to Seattle and Final Days (1994)
xref.body: After escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain took a taxi to LAX and flew back to Seattle on Delta Flight 788. Coincidentally, he sat next to Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan in business class, who later reported Kurt seemed fine and even offered him a ride, which Kurt declined. He signed an autograph and then disappeared. He made it back to his house before 2 AM on Saturday, April 2nd, and was last seen by the Cobains' former nanny, Callie, and her girlfriend around 6 AM that morning. "He took a taxi to LAX and flew back to Seattle on Delta Flight 788. By coincidence, sitting next to him in business class was Guns and Roses bass player Duff McKagan."

xref.title: Dave Kushner Joins Velvet Revolver (2003)
xref.body: Dave Kushner, formerly a member of Wasted Youth, was recruited into the supergroup Velvet Revolver by the ex-Guns N' Roses members. "Plus they had convinced their buddy Dave Kushner for a band called Wasted Youth to join up."

xref.title: Formation as a Supergroup (2003)
xref.body: Formed in 2003, Velvet Revolver began with former Guns N' Roses members Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum, who then recruited Dave Kushner from Wasted Youth. They auditioned several singers, including Josh Todd of Buckcherry, Travis Meeks of Days of the New, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, before settling on Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Former Members Form Velvet Revolver (2003)
xref.body: Three former members of Guns N' Roses – Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum – reconciled and formed a new band, Velvet Revolver, in 2003, eventually recruiting Dave Kushner and Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band. It was Duff, Slash, and drummer Matt Sorom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Velvet Revolver Formation (2003)

xref.title: Manufactured Supergroup (2004)
xref.body: Velvet Revolver was openly acknowledged as a "manufactured product" assembled by managers, essentially a combination of Guns N' Roses members with Scott Weiland and another musician, rather than a naturally formed group. "It was a manufactured product put together as a supergroup by various managers. It was basically guns and roses with Scott Wyland and some other guy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Press Conference Behavior (2004)
xref.body: At a press conference for Velvet Revolver's "Contraband" album, Scott Weiland was notably separate, aloof, and unapproachable, creating palpable tension. In contrast, the former Guns N' Roses members were friendly and engaging. "He exhibited an aloofness that resulted in a puppable tension when he was in the room. And while the rest of the band was only too happy to talk, Wyland was icy cold and completely unapproachable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tense Press Conference Dynamics (2004)
xref.body: At a press conference for the "Contraband" album, the former Guns N' Roses members (Duff, Slash, Matt) were friendly and engaging, while Dave Kushner was quiet. Scott Weiland, however, was totally separate, aloof, and unapproachable, creating palpable tension and doubt about the band's longevity. "He exhibited an aloofness that resulted in a puppable tension when he was in the room. And while the rest of the band was only too happy to talk, Wyland was icy cold and completely unapproachable."

xref.title: Final Texts and Plans (July 2017)
xref.body: In July 2017, while his wife Talinda and six children were on vacation in Arizona, Chester Bennington returned to Los Angeles on July 19, citing a television commercial shoot as the reason. Around the same time, he exchanged texts with Robert DeLeo of Stone Temple Pilots and Matt Sorum of Guns N' Roses, even floating the idea of performing with Sorum again in their band Kings of Chaos, with no alarm bells raised by anyone. "In July 2017, his wife, Talinda, and his family, he had six kids, went to Arizona on a vacation. But then on July 19th, he said he had to get back to LA."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Proposed Reformation (2017)
xref.body: On July 19, 2017, Chester Bennington sent an email to Matt Sorum, the former drummer of Guns N' Roses, expressing his enthusiasm for reforming Kings of Chaos, which he described as an "all-star covers band." This communication occurred less than 24 hours before Chester's death. "On July 19, he sent an email to Matt Sorum, the former drummer with guns and roses, saying that he would like to reform kings of chaos and all-star covers band. That'd be so much fun, he said."

xref.title: Roy Thomas Baker Death (2025) – Producer of Bohemian Rhapsody
xref.body: Roy Thomas Baker, the English producer who guided Queen through their greatest years — including the recording of "Bohemian Rhapsody" — died in 2025 at age 78. He also shaped the distinctive sound of The Cars and worked with artists ranging from David Bowie to Metallica and Guns N' Roses. "Remembered for guiding Queen in their greatest years, including 'Bohemian Rhapsody.'"

xref.title: Biggest Rock Comeback of the 2010s
xref.body: Guns N' Roses, with 60% of their original lineup, reunited for the "Not in This Lifetime... Tour" between 2016 and 2019. This tour grossed nearly $600 million US dollars over 158 shows, making it the fourth-most profitable tour of all time to that point and the biggest rock comeback of the decade. "Even 60% of guns and roses reunited against all odds for the not-in-this-life-type tour, which grossed nearly $600 million US dollars over a hundred and fifty-eight shows played between 2016 and 2019, making it the fourth-most profitable tour of all time to that point." "That was easily the biggest rock come back at the decade."

xref.title: Feud with Guns N' Roses
xref.body: The bad blood between Nirvana and Guns N' Roses, particularly with Axl Rose, started when Kurt Cobain refused an offer for Nirvana to open for Guns N' Roses on a major world tour. Kurt viewed Guns N' Roses as "too big" and was concerned that aligning with them would be perceived as selling out, stating Nirvana was not a "typical Guns n' Roses type of band that has absolutely nothing to say." Axl Rose, who was a fan of Nirvana (even wearing a Nirvana hat in the "Don't Cry" video), felt snubbed and began publicly insulting Kurt and Courtney Love as "junkies," claiming their daughter had birth defects due to their drug use. "It began when Kurt refused an offer by the Gunners to have Nirvana open for them on one of their massive world tours."

Axl Rose, a fan of Nirvana who even wore a Nirvana hat in the "Don't Cry" video, felt insulted and began publicly calling Kurt and Courtney Love "junkies," claiming their daughter had birth defects due to their drug use. xref.title: Influence on Rock Music
xref.body: The Ramones are credited with profoundly influencing countless rock bands over several decades, with a direct lineage tracing back to their original version for bands like Rise Against, Metallica, Blink 182, Motorhead, Green Day, Guns N' Roses, The Clash, Sex Pistols, Rancid, The Pixies, The Beastie Boys, Alice in Chains, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, The Strokes, The Offspring, and Red Hot Chili Peppers. "virtually any rock band of the last 25 years, 35 years, and you can draw a line back into the past, and that line will inevitably lead back to the Ramones."

xref.title: Manic Street Preachers' Self-Comparison
xref.body: The Manic Street Preachers openly stated they felt they had more in common with bands like Guns N' Roses than with the emerging Britpop or Manchester music scene of the early 1990s. This reflected their preference for a more aggressive, American-style rock and roll. "They professed to have more in common with guns and roses in Motley Crew than anything from Manchester or early Britpop, saying that real rock and roll came from America."

xref.title: Reconciliation with Duff McKagan Before Death
xref.body: Days before Kurt Cobain's death, after leaving a rehab center in Los Angeles, he encountered Duff McKagan of Guns N' Roses on a Delta flight back to Seattle. They had a pleasant conversation, and Duff even offered Kurt a ride home from the airport, though Kurt vanished before taking it. "After walking away from a rehab center in Los Angeles, Kurt found himself on a Delta flight back to Seattle, sitting right next to Duff McKagan in business class."

xref.title: Reunion for Touring
xref.body: Guns N' Roses was one of many bands from past decades that reunited in the 21st century, a trend largely motivated by financial incentives. With declining CD sales impacting artist revenues, returning to the touring circuit offered a lucrative way to appeal to nostalgic fan bases and fill large venues. "The list of reunions is long."
